hello.note: Said with palms pressed together, at any time of day. More formal: नमस्कार (namaskaar).

goodbye.note: Literally 'we'll meet again'. नमस्ते (namaste) is also said when leaving.

please.note: Formal. In speech, politeness comes from the -nuhos verb ending (often said -nus) and a soft न (na).

thank_you.note: Nepalis thank less often than English speakers; the English 'thank you' is also widely used.

youre_welcome.note: Literally 'it's nothing' — Nepali has no set reply to thanks.

yes.note: Literally 'it is'. Politer: हजुर (hajur). Often you answer by repeating the question's verb.

no.note: Literally 'it isn't'. For 'there isn't / I don't have', say छैन (chhaina).

sorry.note: For small slips the English 'sorry' is also very common.

excuse_me.note: Literally 'please listen'. You can also call out दाइ (daai, 'brother') or दिदी (didi, 'sister').

good_morning.note: Formal or written; in person most people simply say नमस्ते (namaste).

how_are_you.note: Also very common: सन्चै हुनुहुन्छ? (sanchai hunuhunchha?), 'are you well?'

im_fine.note: To ask back: अनि तपाईंलाई? (ani tapaainlaai?)

my_name_is.note: The verb हो (ho, 'is') comes at the end, after the name.

where_from.note: Also asked: तपाईंको घर कहाँ हो? (tapaainko ghar kahaan ho?), 'where is your home?'

im_from.note: A woman says: म …बाट आएकी हुँ (ma …baata aaeki hun).

speak_english.note: Also natural: तपाईंलाई अङ्ग्रेजी आउँछ? (tapaainlaai angreji aaunchha?)

dont_understand.note: Literally 'I didn't understand' — Nepalis use the past tense here.

speak_slowly.note: न (na) at the end softens a request, like adding 'please'.

what.note: If you didn't catch something, हजुर? (hajur?) is the polite 'pardon?'.

how_much.note: Also common: यो कति हो? (yo kati ho?)

where_bathroom.note: In everyday speech ट्वाइलेट (twaailet) is just as common.

what_time.note: The answer uses the same verb: तीन बज्यो (tin bajyo), 'it's three o'clock'.

what_means.note: Casual: यो भनेको के हो? (yo bhaneko ke ho?)

six.note: Devanagari digit: ६. Sounds the same as छ (chha), 'is'.

tea.note: Usually milky and sweet; black tea is कालो चिया (kaalo chiyaa).

bread.note: Means flatbread; sliced loaf bread is पाउरोटी (paauroti).

im_hungry.note: Thirsty: मलाई तिर्खा लाग्यो (malaai tirkhaa laagyo).

bill_please.note: Also common: हिसाब गरिदिनुहोस् (hisaab garidinuhos), 'please settle the account'.

enjoy_meal.note: Nepali has no fixed 'bon appétit'; hosts say this ('eat heartily').

straight_ahead.note: To a driver: सिधै जानुहोस् (sidhai jaanuhos), 'go straight on'.

stop_here.note: 'Right here' is यहीँ (yahin). Drivers are often called दाइ (daai, 'brother').

airport.note: In everyday speech most people say एयरपोर्ट (eyarport).

hotel.note: Also means a simple restaurant; a cheap place to stay is often a लज (laj).

train_station.note: Nepal has few trains; the bus station is बसपार्क (baspaark).

want_to_go.note: No word for 'to' is needed: मलाई पोखरा जानु छ (malaai pokharaa jaanu chha).

one_ticket.note: When counting things, 'one' is एउटा (eutaa), not एक (ek).

cheaper.note: To bargain: अलि घटाउनुहोस् न (ali ghataaunuhos na), 'lower it a bit'.

pay_card.note: मिल्छ? (milchha?), 'is it possible?', works for asking permission for almost anything.

closed.note: Also the word for a general strike, when shops stay shut.

good_evening.note: Formal or written; in person most people simply say नमस्ते (namaste).

good_night.note: Among friends the English 'good night' is very common.

wait_moment.note: Casual: एक छिन है (ek chhin hai), 'just a sec'.

call_police.note: The official word is प्रहरी (prahari). Police emergency number in Nepal: 100.

im_lost.note: Also: मैले बाटो बिराएँ (maile baato biraaen), 'I've lost my way'.

pharmacy.note: People also say मेडिकल (medikal) or फार्मेसी (faarmesi).

lost_phone.note: If it was stolen: मेरो फोन चोरी भयो (mero fon chori bhayo).

be_careful.note: Gentler, when someone leaves: सम्हालेर जानुहोस् (samhaalera jaanuhos), 'go carefully'.

no_problem.note: Casual: केही छैन (kehi chhaina) or ठिक छ (thik chha).

maybe.note: As a one-word reply, होला (holaa) is very common.

im_tired.note: Also: मलाई थकाइ लाग्यो (malaai thakaai laagyo).

welcome.note: At the door hosts usually say आउनुहोस्, आउनुहोस्! (aaunuhos, aaunuhos!), 'come in'.
